#1806. Pascal Gross: Brighton career assessed after huge contract announcement for “valuable” club legend

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 18:15

Brighton & Hove Albion have announced that Pascal Gross has agreed a new contract with the club until June 2028.

The 35-year-old’s original deal at the Amex Stadium was due to expire at the end of the season, but he has decide to commit his future to the Seagulls by an additional 12 months.

Gross has been rewarded for his talismanic impact back at Brighton since re-joining from boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in January.

The announcement of Gross’s new contract comes ahead of Sunday's Premier League fixture away against Hull City where the midfielder is set to make his 300th club appearance.

"We are really pleased that Pascal has signed a new contract,” head coach Fabian Hurzeler told Brighton’s official website.

"We can talk about his many qualities on the pitch - his goals, assists and football intelligence - but he is also a great leader within the group.

"He connects different generations and different nationalities in our squad. He's so valuable because he helps everyone understand what it takes to be successful."

We are delighted to confirm that Pascal Gross has agreed a new contract with the club! ?

Hurzeler also spoke highly of Gross at his pre-match press conference ahead of their trip to Hull, telling reporters: “He's very adaptive to every personality, and he finds access to every person.

“I think that's something we shouldn't underestimate, and therefore he's so valuable because he gives everyone an understanding of what it needs to be successful.

“No matter if you are 19, 20 years old, no matter if you are 27 or 32, and no matter where you come from, it's all about our standards.

“He's a great standard driver, culture driver, together with Jason (Steele), together with Lewis (Dunk). They are very helpful in driving these things, and therefore I think that's his biggest impact.

“Of course, we can speak about all his goals and assists and football understanding, but being that connector beside the pitch is very valuable.”

Gross stands out as arguably Brighton’s greatest modern signing, evolving from a bargain £3m arrival in 2017 into the club's all-time Premier League goalscorer and creative heartbeat since returning earlier this year.

Across two spells at the club, Gross’s tactical intelligence and versatility has allowed him to excel in a variety of midfield positions under four different permanent managers - Chris Hughton, Graham Potter, Roberto De Zerbi and now Hurzeler.

Renowned as one of the top-flight's premier set-piece specialists and chance creators, Gross has amassed 35 goals and 52 assists in 257 Premier League appearances - the joint-highest total of goal involvements by a German player in the division’s history.

His decisive contributions famously secured Brighton's top-flight survival in 2018, propelled them to a historic sixth-place European finish in 2023, and continue to drive their 2026-27 campaign, with the Seagulls currently sitting second in the table after 10 games.

Cemented as an undisputed Brighton legend, Gross has recorded four goals and four assists in 10 league outings this term and was voted Premier League Player of the Month in September.

#1805. Pavlovic admits he jokes about retiring with Moreira at Partizan: “He’s a fantastic guy”

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has spoken about potentially retiring alongside Diego Moreira in the future, after a new revelation.

It’s clear that, since he’s arrived, Moreira has had a huge impact on the dressing room. In terms of quality, Mark van Bommel called him ‘crazy’, but compared him to Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, Koni De Winter repeated similar sentiments today, saying that he may be a little crazy, but he was a good character to be around and a great footballer and Milan fans can see this, too. The Belgian is already making the €50 million paid for him look like a bargain and he has plenty of room left for growth.

Speaking to SS Calcio, Pavlovic looked at his relationship with Moreira, the help from Massimiliano Allegri last season and who gave him the most difficult game in his career, as MilanPress relayed.

“Working with Allegri was beneficial for me. It’s under his guidance that I’ve made the most progress since arriving in Italy. As a central defender, I possess good speed, strength, and skill with the ball.

“I can pass the ball forward and score goals, but tactical skills have always been a weakness of mine. I only learned the basics when I joined the first team at Partizan. Given the way Italians view football, I was a bit behind the times, as their players begin to grasp certain concepts from a very young age.”

“Physically, the toughest challenge was undoubtedly against Romelu Lukaku. But also Marcus Thuram: he’s strong, quick, and very skilled with the ball at his feet. With Lautaro, however, you have to be very careful inside the penalty area: if you don’t stay close to him, he’ll score.

The bond that unites Moreira and Pavlovic…

“I didn’t even know he was Almami’s son [a former Partizan player]. He’s a fantastic guy, really smart. He knows a few bits of Serbian. I met his father during a training session. We talked about Partizan, of course. It was really nice to see him; I remember him from his time at Partizan.”

The possibility of joining Partizan at the end of his career…

“I often joke with Moreira, telling him that, at the end of our careers, we should play at least one season at Partizan. I point out that I’m three years older than him, so he’ll have to make a small sacrifice so we can get back together. He’s a truly great guy.

“There’s a fantastic atmosphere in our group. It’s a real pleasure to be part of Milan.”

#1804. Fernandes: Not the right time for Man Utd contract talks

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has put contract talks on hold.

The Red Devils, who have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, sit in the Premier League relegation zone ahead of facing Liverpool on Sunday.

Fernandes, who was the standout performer in the Premier League last term, has not been at his usual best.

However, the Portugal international has still contributed directly to nine goals in 14 games (six goals, three assists), while only four players in the Premier League can better his 23 chances created this term.

Fernandes' deal expires at the end of the season, but even though United have offered him a new contract, the 32-year-old has paused those negotiations.

"The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 21, 2026

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

#1803. Augsburg vs Mainz 05 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:54

Augsburg's WWK Arena will be the backdrop for their clash with Mainz 05 on Sunday in a potentially pivotal clash in the battle against relegation.

The home side are 14th in the Bundesliga table with nine points, whereas their opponents are 12th with 10, and a loss for either could leave them in the bottom three.

Augsburg are only two points above 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the relegation playoff spot, while they are just three points ahead of 17th-placed Schalke 04.

The hosts are winless in their past seven league matches, a period in which they claimed just three points and suffered four defeats.

Head coach Manuel Baum will not be pleased that his team conceded at least two goals in six of those fixtures, though he will highlight that the club netted 13 times in that stretch.

Fuggerstadter have played five contests at WWK Arena in 2026-27, and they have triumphed once, drawn three times and won once at the stadium.

Two of those stalemates came against Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen, while their only defeat at home came against third-placed Freiburg at the end of October.

The visitors come into the clash looking to avoid a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions, and avoid losing a fourth straight Bundesliga game.

Perhaps the saving grace for Mainz is that the rest of the bottom seven play teams currently in the top eight, meaning it is unlikely that they will end the weekend in the relegation zone.

Urs Fischer's side did score four goals in their four losses, but they conceded on 11 occasions, and their latest defeat saw them ship twice when they lost 2-1 against Bayern Munich on November 7.

Mainz's record on the road has been largely positive this term, as while they were beaten 4-1 by Elversberg on October 30, they did emerge as winners in their first three away Bundesliga outings of the campaign.

The club are also unbeaten in their five most recent meetings with Augsburg, claiming victory four times, including when they won 2-0 in February.

Augsburg only have two confirmed absentees, with Han-Noah Massengo and defender Chrislain Matsima ruled out.

Juma Bah, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw and Yannik Keitel could be trusted together in defence, while Robin Fellhauer and Fabian Rieder may start in a double pivot.

Striker Michael Gregoritsch has scored five times in the league this season, and he is certain to lead the line, supported by Anton Kade and Alexis Claude-Maurice.

Though Mainz only have to contend with the absence of centre-back Dominik Kohr, he is not scheduled to return until January because of an ankle injury.

Stefan Posch, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are likely candidates to start in the team's back three, and the trio may be protected by Paul Nebel and Kaishu Sano from midfield.

Dahmen; Bah, Gouweleeuw, Keitel; Wolf, Fellhauer, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Claude-Maurice; Gregoritsch

Zentner; Posch, Gruber, Potulski; Caci, Nebel, Sano, Amiri, Mwene; Tietz, Becker

Neither Augsburg nor Mainz have been particularly strong defensively, so it would be surprising if either kept a clean sheet.

The hosts boast the advantage of playing at WWK Arena, but the visitors have often travelled well, and the two may ultimately have to settle for a point on Sunday.

#1802. The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010)

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

#1801. Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the issue with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager said.

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic."

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively new challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

"It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place."

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret."

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the issue is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's new restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

#1800. Kovac: Nmecha’s winner ‘lucky’ but Dortmund deserving victors

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Niko Kovac believes Borussia Dortmund deserved their 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach, though he conceded that Felix Nmecha's 80th-minute winner was fortunate.

Following Bayern Munich's 2-2 draw with Koln on Friday, Kovac's side capitalised to move top of the Bundesliga and open up a two-point lead over their rivals.

Dortmund dominated the early exchanges at Borussia-Park, with Nmecha, Nico Schlotterbeck and Jobe Bellingham going close to breaking the deadlock.

Robin Hack and Joe Scally threatened for Monchengladbach at the other end, but it was Nmecha who ultimately settled the contest in the 80th minute, with his powerful, low 20-yard strike ricocheting off a helpless Daniel Batz and into the roof of the net.

"Based on our second-half performance, I think we deserved to win," Kovac told reporters. "But, of course, it was still a lucky goal from Felix.

"After the international break, it's always very important to start with a win. Gladbach did really well defensively. The opponent was very tenacious and very aggressive.

"We weren't able to impose our game in the first half as much as we did in the second.

"In the second half, we seized control of the game, partly through our substitutions, and then controlled and dominated the match."

— Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 21, 2026

Kovac's side are now unbeaten across their opening 10 Bundesliga matches for just the third time in club history, after 2002-03 and 2018-19.

Following Saturday's win, they have recorded 24 points – just one short of their record haul at this stage, set in 2010-11 and matched again in 2013-14.

Nmecha, meanwhile, has emerged as a pivotal key to Dortmund's success, leading the Black-Yellow for goals this season (five), having now scored in consecutive Bundesliga appearances for the first time.

"We weren't sharp enough in the first half. We gave the ball away too easily," Nmecha conceded.

"We were better in the second half, and we're happy to have got three points. It's still a very long season.

"We don't want to look at others but simply have to continue the way we're doing now: focusing on ourselves. Hopefully, we'll get as many points as possible."

#1799. Romano states Milan could be an option for Balde with Mendes links: “Discuss a strategy”

According to Fabrizio Romano, AC Milan could be involved in the market for Alejandro Balde once again this winter.

A central defender would be the main target for most Milan fans ahead of the winter mercato, but the possibility of signing another wing-back wouldn’t be turned down. In fact, with the left-side still proving to be a puzzling area, someone may need to be recruited.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the past, Balde has been linked and there have been several other suggestions. However, the Spaniard may be the most accessible mid-way through the season and it would seem that the Rossoneri are considering him again.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Romano looked at the left-back’s future and didn’t deny that the Diavolo could be involved for another mercato, as MilanNews relayed.

“In the last few hours, Barcelona’s sporting director Deco spoke about Alejandro Balde and said that they are not planning on Balde’s exit because we are only in mid-November; there is a month and a half to go until January.

“Barça play every two or three days and a player like Balde can clearly still be useful between now and the transfer market. It’s true that Barça has left-back cover at the moment, but Barça doesn’t want to put a player like Balde on the market publicly already in mid-November.

“The reality behind the scenes is different: Balde remains a player who could leave in January, because Jorge Mendes, the player’s agent, was in Barcelona this week to speak with the player and discuss a strategy.

“Balde could therefore leave, but we must be realistic because there are significant figures at stake, given that he earns more than €5 million net and in the summer Barcelona were asking for €50 million for him.

“We’ll see if the formula can change in January, but on the one hand, Deco says so, on the other, there’s the reality: if Balde doesn’t play as well as he hasn’t been playing between now and January, the idea of ​​Balde leaving could become concrete.

“We told you that he’s currently being offered to Roma, but the Giallorossi haven’t really picked up steam yet. They’ve also offered him to Milan; the player was initially proposed last summer, but without a transfer, nothing happened.

“We’ll see what happens with Alejandro Balde, but he’s a name for the international or possibly Italian market that we need to keep there.”

Considering Sankhoun Diawara is now being considered as a left-back, the situation is certainly not ideal. So, Milan could certainly do worse than signing Balde.

#1798. £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

At least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx

Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

#1797. Brentford news: Keith Andrews confirms double injury blow ahead of Everton meeting

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 19:13, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:13

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Aaron Hickey and Nathan Collins will be out for a "number of weeks".

Hickey was forced off with a hamstring injury in the first half of Scotland's 4-0 defeat against Switzerland in Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The full-back, who has a history of hamstring problems, is now set for a spell on the sidelines along with Nathan Collins, who missed the Republic of Ireland's 3-0 win over Kosovo with a knee issue.

“No, they won't be available for a number of weeks,” Andrews said when he spoke to reporters ahead of Monday's Premier League meeting with Everton.

“I was actually watching Aaron's game as it happened and I'm just so bitterly disappointed for him.

“He's had such a painful journey on that front with injury, so it's really disappointing for him.

“Similarly with Nathan, he's obviously had a period out with his calf. He's done really well to get back ahead of schedule and played a couple of games.

“These international games came at a really good time for him to get good game time and obviously represent his country, and unfortunately he's hurt his knee. Nathan will be out for a couple of weeks or so.”

Brentford are also without the first-choice striker Igor Thiago, who will serve a three-match ban after being sent off in the 2-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international window.

The Bees are also without the injured duo of Rico Henry and Kaye Furo, while Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo are not ready to return to first-team action despite making progress in their respective recoveries.

In positive news, Andrews has revealed Fabio Carvalho has "every chance" of featuring in Monday's squad after missing the last four games through injury.

Brentford head into the weekend in eighth place in the Premier League table, but they are not in the best of form after winning just one of their last five league games.

#1796. Ajax vs. ADO Den Haag - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how new boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

#1795. Real Madrid ‘pushed themselves to the limit’ in tough win over Celta Vigo

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jose Mourinho did not expect Celta Vigo to pose quite as much of a challenge to Real Madrid as they did, but was delighted with how his team pushed themselves to the maximum.

Madrid fell behind to Pablo Duran's sixth-minute goal, but second-half efforts from Jude Bellingham and Carlos Espi got Los Blancos over the line, while Kylian Mbappe missed a penalty.

Mourinho felt Madrid's performance levels were impacted by so many of their players having arduous journeys over the international break.

But he was delighted with how they kept pushing themselves to get the result.

"I thought it was going to be a tough match, but not this tough. I didn't expect to win it the way we did, but we were up against a good team that played really well," he said.

"Some of us arrived on Monday, others on Tuesday, others on Thursday. Some were on a plane for 12 hours. Normally, after international duty, the ideal is to play on Sunday, but we couldn't because we play [in the Champions League] next Tuesday.

"I saw some players who were physically exhausted, but I also saw some who pushed themselves to the limit. That's the strength of the group, of a group of friends who want to win."

Good morning, Madridistas! https://t.co/ovoL9Li7Q5

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 22, 2026

Espi stepped off the bench to become Madrid's matchwinner.

He is yet to start a LaLiga match for Madrid, but he has scored three goals in 44 minutes played in LaLiga 2026-27, a ratio of one goal every 15 minutes, the best in the top five European leagues among players with at least three goals scored.

However, Mourinho says the 21-year-old is satisfied with a super-sub role for now.

"There are players with specific characteristics," he said.

"I don't want to say he can't be a starter, but Carlos is a penalty-box striker, not so much a link-up player. He's a guy who has quality in the box, who attacks the near post and the far post well, who plays with his back to goal.

"The history of football is full of decisive players like him who didn't play much. He's the kind of guy who doesn't get caught up in stories about needing to play more; he's happy to be at Real Madrid and has the respect of his coach, his team-mates, and the fans.

"He's happy, and I hope to be able to give him starting or regular starting positions."

Vinicius Junior also had to settle for a cameo from the bench, but Mourinho headed off any questions over the Brazilian's status.

"So you don't ask me on Monday, I'll tell you now: he's going to start on Tuesday [against PSV]," Mourinho said of Vinicius.
